name: TENNIS 40:40 HISTORY-FIRST v1.1 DRAFT · IN-PLAY SIGNAL + STATS · FREE-TIER PROVIDER WIRED

parameters.content:
## TENNIS "40:40 – DA" ADAPTATION · v1.1 · FREE-TIER PROVIDER WIRED
This is a fresh in-play signal engine for the manual strategy "Будет в гейме счет 40:40 – ДА" (tennis, live/in-play), NOT a port of the football/hockey Module A pre-match Dixon-Coles engine — the market and the data shape are completely different (per-game deuce pattern inside a live match, not a pre-match goal model).

**Strategy criteria this encodes (from the source notes):**
1. Final or semifinal only (evenly matched opponents produce the pattern most reliably).
2. Watch at least 5-6 completed games before considering any signal (MIN_HISTORY_GAMES).
3. Work out which player's OWN service games keep reaching 40:40 — the bet is that the SAME thing happens on their very next service game. The default threshold (MIN_SIGNAL_RATE = 1.0) requires it to have happened in every one of that player's service games so far, matching the "always" language in the source notes and the worked example (2 out of 2 = 100%, flagged as an "ideal signal").

**Free data source (chosen because it's genuinely free to start): livetennisapi.com**
- Free key: 30 req/min, 100 req/DAY, no card (https://livetennisapi.com/subscribe/free).
- Free tier gives `GET /matches?status=live` (round, players, current server) and `GET /matches/{id}/score` — a POINT-IN-TIME SNAPSHOT of the live score (current set/game number, server, and the point score as "0"/"15"/"30"/"40"/"AD"). It does NOT include game-by-game history — that (`/history/matches/{id}`) is Basic-tier ($9.99/mo) only.
- **So this workflow builds its own history**, by polling the snapshot repeatedly and recording, per (match, set, game), whether the score was ever seen at 40:40/AD (i.e. reached deuce). When the live `game` number moves on, the previous game is finalized from OUR OWN polling log — see the `tennis_4040_games_v1` table below. This has been sanity-checked against the worked Nadal–Fognini example (see script `sim.js` used during development) and reproduces it exactly: games 2 & 4 (Fognini serving) both flagged as deuce, game 6 signaled with ideal_signal=true.
- **Quota math**: each poll = 1 request to list live matches + 1 per eligible (Final/Semifinal) match's score snapshot. With the Schedule Trigger below set to every 3 minutes, a ~2.5h final uses roughly 50 polls × ~2 requests ≈ 100/day — right at the free daily cap for ONE match. Consequences: (a) you can realistically track one live Final/Semifinal at a time on the free key, not several in parallel; (b) a 3-minute gap can miss a deuce that resolves quickly, so recall is imperfect on free — acceptable for validating the pipeline, not for production accuracy. Once the logic is proven, upgrading to Basic ($9.99/mo) unlocks the real `/history/matches/{id}` endpoint, which needs only ~1 call per finished game instead of continuous polling and removes this whole reconstruction step.
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <key>` against `https://api.livetennisapi.com/api/public/v1` per their OpenAPI spec (https://github.com/livetennisapi/openapi). Field names below (`players.p1.name`, `score.p1`, etc.) are taken from that spec — double-check them against the live Swagger/OpenAPI docs when you wire your real key, in case the schema has moved on since this draft was written.

**What you still need to supply before this fires a live signal:**
1. Your free API key from livetennisapi.com, dropped into the KEY constant below.
2. Two Supabase tables (separate from the football/hockey settlement tables):
   - `tennis_4040_games_v1`: match_id, set_num, game_num, server (1/2), server_name, seen_deuce (bool), finalized (bool), created_at, updated_at — unique on (match_id, set_num, game_num). This is the self-built history log described above.
   - `tennis_4040_signals_v1`: id, match_id, set_num, game_num, tournament, round, player_a, player_b, server_name, opponent_name, games_played, server_samples, server_hit_rate, opponent_samples, opponent_hit_rate, odds_estimate, ideal_signal, status [pending/hit/miss], created_at, settled_at.
3. Your own Telegram bot credentials wired into a real Send node (not included here — this draft stops at building the message text) and, for the stats command, a Telegram Trigger with a filter on the "📊 Статистика сигналов" button/text.
4. A paper-trading period. The example in the source material is 5 signals (4 hits) — far too small a sample to trust; the "100% history → signal" heuristic and the reasoning-text thresholds are a reasonable encoding of the manual strategy but are UNVALIDATED at scale, and free-tier polling will further shrink your sample by missing some fast deuces.

**Stats formulas (reproduce the existing bot's numbers exactly):**
- Winrate % = hits / total * 100
- Breakeven % = 1 / REFERENCE_ODDS * 100 (a configured reference price for this bet type, e.g. ~3.10 — NOT the average of the actual signal odds, which vary game to game)
- Edge over the line = Winrate % − Breakeven % (simple percentage-point difference)
These match the screenshot exactly: 80.0% winrate, 32.3% breakeven @3.10, +47.7% edge.

Until the items above are in place, treat every output as a diagnostic, not a bet.
